records.source: לְדָוִ֨ד׀בָּרֲכִ֣י נַ֭פְשִׁי אֶת־יְהוָ֑ה וְכָל־קְ֝רָבַ֗י אֶת־שֵׁ֥ם קָדְשֽׁוֹ׃
records.gloss: Of David. Bless YHWH, my soul, and all my inward parts, [bless] his holy name.
pieces: Of David. Bless {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, my soul; let all that is deep within me bless {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy name.

L.1: Of David. Bless {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, my soul, and all my inward parts, [bless] {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy name.

R.1: By David. With all that I am, I praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. With everything inside me I praise {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy name.

decisions.reason: This psalm's title is short and the Hebrew counts it together with the first line as verse 1, so here the verse numbers are the same as in Bibles that print the title without a number.
To bless (barakh) God is to praise him and thank him, speaking of the good he is and does. When God blesses people he gives them good; when people bless God they give him praise.

decisions.choice: Bless the LORD, my soul: the psalmist calls on himself
decisions.reason: The soul (nefesh) is the whole living self. The psalmist speaks to himself and stirs up all that he is to praise (42:6). The call opens and closes this psalm (verses 1-2, 22) and Psalm 104 (104:1, 35).

decisions.choice: my inward parts: all that is within me
decisions.reason: The word (qerev) is the inside of the body, the seat of thought and feeling; with "all" it means the whole inner self.
Literal and Balanced keep the familiar call to "my soul" in this refrain, since the psalmist is speaking to himself (m2); Readable says it plainly.

decisions.choice: With all that I am, I praise the LORD
decisions.reason: Readable says what the call to one's own soul means: the psalmist praises God with his whole self. The line is the same each time it comes (103:1, 2, 22; 104:1, 35).
As in 11:1 and 3:1.

records.heading: Bless {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, my soul

records.source: בָּרֲכִ֣י נַ֭פְשִׁי אֶת־יְהוָ֑ה וְאַל־תִּ֝שְׁכְּחִ֗י כָּל־גְּמוּלָֽיו׃
records.gloss: Bless YHWH, my soul, and do not forget all his benefits,
pieces: Bless {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, my soul, and never forget all that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has done for you,

L.2: Bless {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, my soul, and do not forget all {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} benefits,

R.2: With all that I am, I praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. I will never forget all the good things {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} does for me.

decisions.choice: his benefits: what he has done
decisions.reason: The word (gemul) is what someone has done to another, here all God's kind dealings, which verses 3-5 go on to list.
Verses 3-5 describe the LORD in a series of "who" phrases, so verses 2-4 end with a comma at Literal and Balanced.

decisions.choice: With all that I am, I praise the LORD
decisions.reason: As in 103:1.

decisions.choice: I will never forget; for me
decisions.reason: The psalmist is speaking to his own soul, that is, to himself (m2 on 103:1), so Readable says "I" and "me" through verse 5.

records.source: הַסֹּלֵ֥חַ לְכָל־עֲוֺנֵ֑כִי הָ֝רֹפֵ֗א לְכָל־תַּחֲלֻאָֽיְכִי׃
records.gloss: who forgives all your iniquity, who heals all your diseases,
pieces: who pardons all your wrongdoing, who cures every illness you have,

L.3: who forgives all your iniquity, who heals all your diseases,

R.3: He forgives all my sins. He heals all my sicknesses.

decisions.choice: forgives all your iniquity: pardons all guilt
decisions.reason: The verb (salach) is used only of God forgiving. Iniquity ('avon) is wrongdoing and the guilt it brings.

decisions.choice: heals all your diseases: healing of body and life
decisions.reason: Forgiveness and healing stand side by side, as in 41:5 and Exodus 15:26: God restores the whole person.
As in 103:2.

records.source: הַגּוֹאֵ֣ל מִשַּׁ֣חַת חַיָּ֑יְכִי הַֽ֝מְעַטְּרֵ֗כִי חֶ֣סֶד וְרַחֲמִֽים׃
records.gloss: who redeems from [the] pit your life, who crowns you [with] loyal love and compassion,
pieces: who ransoms your life from the grave, who makes loyal love and compassion your crown,

L.4: who redeems your life from the pit, who crowns you [with] loyal love and compassion,

R.4: He saves my life from the grave. His faithful love and kindness are like a crown {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} puts on my head.

decisions.reason: The verb (ga'al) is what a close relative did in buying back a family member or land (Leviticus 25:25); God acts as the one who frees his own.
The pit (shachat) is the grave and the world of the dead (16:10; 30:10).
The word (chesed) is the love that keeps faith, God's commitment to his people that does not give up (5:8).
A crown is a sign of honor (8:6). God's love and compassion are the honor he gives.
As in the earlier psalms, Readable says "faithful love" for chesed.
As in 103:2.

records.source: הַמַּשְׂבִּ֣יַע בַּטּ֣וֹב עֶדְיֵ֑ךְ תִּתְחַדֵּ֖שׁ כַּנֶּ֣שֶׁר נְעוּרָֽיְכִי׃
records.gloss: who satisfies with good your ornament; your youth renews itself like the eagle.
pieces: who fills your life with good things, so that you are made young again like the eagle.

L.5: who satisfies your ornament with good, [so that] your youth renews itself like the eagle.

R.5: He fills my life with good things. He makes me young and strong again, like an eagle.

decisions.choice: your ornament: your life, your desire
decisions.reason: The word ('adi) usually means an ornament, which does not fit here. It may be a poetic word for the self (like "my glory" in 16:9) or mean "your years"; the ancient Greek translation reads "your desire". The sense is that God fills the whole of life with good.
The bird (nesher) is the eagle or the great vulture, a picture of strength and long life (Isaiah 40:31).
Balanced and Readable give the likely sense of the obscure word (m1).

records.source: עֹשֵׂ֣ה צְדָק֣וֹת יְהוָ֑ה וּ֝מִשְׁפָּטִ֗ים לְכָל־עֲשׁוּקִֽים׃
records.gloss: Doing righteous acts [is] YHWH, and judgments for all [the] oppressed.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} acts to set things right and gives justice to all who are crushed by others.

L.6: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} does righteous acts, and judgments for all [the] oppressed.

R.6: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} does what is right. He makes sure that people who are treated badly get justice.

decisions.choice: righteous acts: acts that put things right
decisions.reason: The plural (tsedaqot) is used of God's acts of rescue for his people (Judges 5:11; Micah 6:5). He does right by setting the wronged free.

decisions.choice: judgments: justice, verdicts in their favor
decisions.reason: The plural (mishpatim) here is the justice God does: he rules in favor of those who are cheated and oppressed (146:7).

records.source: יוֹדִ֣יעַ דְּרָכָ֣יו לְמֹשֶׁ֑ה לִבְנֵ֥י יִ֝שְׂרָאֵ֗ל עֲלִילֽוֹתָיו׃
records.gloss: He made known his ways to Moses, to [the] children of Israel his deeds.
pieces: He let Moses know {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} ways and let the people of Israel see what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} could do.

L.7: He made known {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} ways to Moses, to the children of Israel {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} deeds.

R.7: He taught Moses how {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} works. He showed the people of Israel the great things {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} did.

decisions.reason: Moses prayed, "Let me know your ways" (Exodus 33:13), and God answered by passing before him and proclaiming his name, the words verse 8 repeats (Exodus 34:6).

decisions.choice: his ways, his deeds: who he is and what he does
decisions.reason: His ways are how he acts and what he is like; his deeds are the great acts Israel saw, as in the exodus.

records.source: רַח֣וּם וְחַנּ֣וּן יְהוָ֑ה אֶ֖רֶךְ אַפַּ֣יִם וְרַב־חָֽסֶד׃
records.gloss: Compassionate and gracious [is] YHWH, slow of anger and great of loyal love.
pieces: Tender and gracious is {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, slow to anger, rich in loyal love.

L.8: Compassionate and gracious [is] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, slow to anger and great in loyal love.

R.8: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is kind and full of mercy. He is patient and does not get angry quickly. His faithful love is great.

decisions.reason: This is the LORD's own description of himself to Moses (Exodus 34:6), often echoed in the Psalms and the prophets (86:15; 145:8; Jonah 4:2).
Literally "long of nostrils": the anger that shows in the face takes a long time to rise.
The word (chesed) is the love that keeps faith, God's commitment to his people that does not give up (5:8).
As in the earlier psalms, Readable says "faithful love" for chesed.

records.source: לֹֽא־לָנֶ֥צַח יָרִ֑יב וְלֹ֖א לְעוֹלָ֣ם יִטּֽוֹר׃
records.gloss: Not forever will he contend, and not forever will he keep [anger].
pieces: He does not keep bringing charges, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} does not hold on to anger for all time.

L.9: Not forever will {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} contend, and not forever will {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} keep [anger].

R.9: He will not always be finding fault with us. He will not stay angry forever.

decisions.reason: The verb (riv) is to bring a charge in court. God does bring his people to account, but not without end (Isaiah 57:16).
The verb (natar) is used without an object, but it means to keep anger, to bear a grudge (Jeremiah 3:5, 12; Leviticus 19:18).
All three levels supply the object of the verb (m2); Literal brackets it.

records.source: לֹ֣א כַ֭חֲטָאֵינוּ עָ֣שָׂה לָ֑נוּ וְלֹ֥א כַ֝עֲוֺנֹתֵ֗ינוּ גָּמַ֥ל עָלֵֽינוּ׃
records.gloss: Not according to our sins has he dealt with us, and not according to our iniquities has he repaid us.
pieces: He has not treated us as our sins called for, nor paid us back in full for our wrongs.

L.10: Not according to our sins has {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} dealt with us, and not according to our iniquities has {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} repaid us.

R.10: He does not punish us as much as our sins deserve. He does not pay us back for all the wrong we have done.

decisions.reason: The verse does not say that sin does not matter; it says that God's mercy goes beyond strict payment for it (130:3-4; Ezra 9:13).

records.source: כִּ֤י כִגְבֹ֣הַּ שָׁ֭מַיִם עַל־הָאָ֑רֶץ גָּבַ֥ר חַ֝סְדּ֗וֹ עַל־יְרֵאָֽיו׃
records.gloss: For as [the] heavens are high above the earth, [so] is strong his loyal love over [those] fearing him.
pieces: As far as the sky towers over the earth, so mighty is {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} loyal love over all who fear {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

L.11: For as the heavens are high above the earth, [so] strong is {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} loyal love over those who fear {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

R.11: The sky is very high above the earth. That is how great {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} faithful love is for people who honor {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.reason: The verb (gavar) means to be strong, to prevail. God's love is as far above his people as the sky is above the earth, and it overcomes their sin (verse 12).
The word (chesed) is the love that keeps faith, God's commitment to his people that does not give up (5:8).

decisions.choice: those who fear him: who revere and trust him
decisions.reason: The fear of God is reverence that leads to trust and obedience (25:14; 34:10).
As in the earlier psalms, Readable says "faithful love" for chesed.
As in the earlier psalms, Readable says "honor" for the fear that is reverence and trust (25:14), not terror.

records.source: כִּרְחֹ֣ק מִ֭זְרָח מִֽמַּֽעֲרָ֑ב הִֽרְחִ֥יק מִ֝מֶּ֗נּוּ אֶת־פְּשָׁעֵֽינוּ׃
records.gloss: As far as east [is] from west, [so] far he has removed from us our transgressions.
pieces: As distant as sunrise is from sunset, so distant has {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} set our rebellious acts from us.

L.12: As far as east [is] from west, [so] far {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has removed our transgressions from us.

R.12: He has carried our sins away from us, as far as the place where the sun rises is from where it sets.

decisions.choice: east, west: the place of sunrise and of sunset
decisions.reason: The words (mizrach, ma'arav) mean where the sun comes up and where it goes down: the farthest distance anyone could see.
The word (pesha') is rebellion against God, a breaking of faith with him (32:1; 51:3).
Balanced gives the picture in the words (m1).

records.source: כְּרַחֵ֣ם אָ֭ב עַל־בָּנִ֑ים רִחַ֥ם יְ֝הוָ֗ה עַל־יְרֵאָֽיו׃
records.gloss: As a father has compassion on [his] children, [so] YHWH has compassion on [those] fearing him.
pieces: Just as a father feels for his children, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} feels tender love for all who fear {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

L.13: As a father has compassion on [his] children, [so] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has compassion on those who fear {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

R.13: A father is kind and gentle to his children. In the same way {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is kind and gentle to people who honor {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.reason: The verb (richam) is a deep, tender love, like that of a parent; it is related to the word for the womb (Isaiah 49:15).
The Old Testament calls God the father of his people in a few places (Deuteronomy 32:6; Jeremiah 31:9); here the picture is of his gentle care.
As in the earlier psalms, Readable says "honor" for the fear that is reverence and trust (25:14), not terror.

records.source: כִּי־ה֖וּא יָדַ֣ע יִצְרֵ֑נוּ זָ֝כ֗וּר כִּי־עָפָ֥ר אֲנָֽחְנוּ׃
records.gloss: For he knows our form; [he is] remembering that dust [are] we.
pieces: For {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} knows what we are made of; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} does not forget that we are only dust.

L.14: For {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} knows our form; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} remembers that we [are] dust.

R.14: He knows how {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} formed us. He remembers that we are made from dust.

decisions.reason: God formed (yatsar) the first human from the dust of the ground (Genesis 2:7) and said, "you are dust" (Genesis 3:19). The word for form (yetser) comes from the same root.

decisions.choice: our form: how we are made
decisions.reason: The word (yetser) is something formed, as a potter forms clay; in Genesis 6:5 the same word is the bent of the heart. Here it is our frail make-up.

records.source: אֱ֭נוֹשׁ כֶּחָצִ֣יר יָמָ֑יו כְּצִ֥יץ הַ֝שָּׂדֶ֗ה כֵּ֣ן יָצִֽיץ׃
records.gloss: Humankind, like grass [are] his days; like a flower of the field, so he flourishes,
pieces: Mortals have days like grass; they bloom like a flower in the open field,

L.15: {{gender:A mortal|Man}} — like grass [are] {{gender:their|his}} days; like a flower of the field, so {{gender:they flourish|he flourishes}},

R.15: Human life is short, like grass. People bloom like wild flowers.

decisions.choice: humankind: human beings, weak and mortal
decisions.reason: The word ('enosh) means a human being, often with a sense of weakness (8:5; 90:3).

decisions.choice: grass, a flower of the field: life that soon fades
decisions.reason: In a dry land grass and wild flowers spring up after rain and wither in days (90:5-6; Isaiah 40:6-8).

decisions.choice: a mortal, their, they flourish (with "man", "his", "he flourishes" as the alternatives)
decisions.reason: The word means any human being (m1), so Literal gives inclusive wording by default with the traditional words as the alternative (8:5); Balanced and Readable say "mortals" and "people".

records.source: כִּ֤י ר֣וּחַ עָֽבְרָה־בּ֣וֹ וְאֵינֶ֑נּוּ וְלֹא־יַכִּירֶ֖נּוּ ע֣וֹד מְקוֹמֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: for a wind passes over it, and it is not, and its place does not recognize it again.
pieces: a wind blows across it and it has vanished; its own place will not know it again.

L.16: for a wind passes over it, and it is not, and its place no longer knows it.

R.16: Then the hot wind blows over them, and they are gone. No one even remembers where they were.

decisions.choice: a wind: the hot desert wind
decisions.reason: The burning east wind from the desert can wither plants in a day (Isaiah 40:7; Ezekiel 17:10).

decisions.choice: its place does not know it: no trace is left
decisions.reason: The place where it grew does not recognize it again: it is gone without trace (Job 7:10).
Readable names the kind of wind (m1) and speaks of the people the flowers stand for.

records.source: וְחֶ֤סֶד יְהוָ֨ה׀מֵעוֹלָ֣ם וְעַד־ע֭וֹלָם עַל־יְרֵאָ֑יו וְ֝צִדְקָת֗וֹ לִבְנֵ֥י בָנִֽים׃
records.gloss: But [the] loyal love of YHWH [is] from everlasting and to everlasting on [those] fearing him, and his righteousness to children of children,
pieces: But the loyal love of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} lasts from age to age on all who fear {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, while {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} righteousness reaches their children's children,

L.17: But the loyal love of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [is] from everlasting to everlasting on those who fear {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} righteousness to children's children,

R.17: But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s faithful love lasts forever and ever for people who honor {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. He will do what is right for their grandchildren too.

decisions.reason: The word (chesed) is the love that keeps faith, God's commitment to his people that does not give up (5:8).

decisions.choice: from everlasting to everlasting: unlike human days
decisions.reason: Human life is as short as grass (verses 15-16); God's love has no beginning and no end (90:2), and it reaches the generations to come (Exodus 20:6).

decisions.choice: his righteousness: his faithful saving acts
decisions.reason: God's righteousness (tsedaqah) here is his faithfulness in doing right by his people, as in verse 6.
As in the earlier psalms, Readable says "faithful love" for chesed.
As in the earlier psalms, Readable says "honor" for the fear that is reverence and trust (25:14), not terror.

records.source: לְשֹׁמְרֵ֥י בְרִית֑וֹ וּלְזֹכְרֵ֥י פִ֝קֻּדָ֗יו לַעֲשׂוֹתָֽם׃
records.gloss: to [those who] keep his covenant and to [those who] remember his precepts to do them.
pieces: for all who hold to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} covenant and are careful to carry out what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} commands.

L.18: to those who keep {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} covenant and to those who remember {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} precepts, to do them.

R.18: That love is for people who are faithful to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} covenant and remember to do what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says.

decisions.reason: The word (piqqudim) is used only in the Psalms, of God's specific instructions (19:9; 119:4).
God's lasting love is given to those who keep faith with him in the covenant, remembering his words in order to live by them (Deuteronomy 7:9).

records.source: יְֽהוָ֗ה בַּ֭שָּׁמַיִם הֵכִ֣ין כִּסְא֑וֹ וּ֝מַלְכוּת֗וֹ בַּכֹּ֥ל מָשָֽׁלָה׃
records.gloss: YHWH in the heavens has established his throne, and his kingdom over all rules.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has fixed {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} throne in heaven; {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} royal power reigns over all there is.

L.19: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has established {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} throne in the heavens, and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} kingdom rules over all.

R.19: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has made heaven the place of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} throne. He is King over everything.

decisions.choice: his kingdom over all: the LORD as King
decisions.reason: The call to praise in verses 20-22 rests on this: the LORD is King of everything, in heaven and on earth (93:1; 97:1).

records.source: בָּרֲכ֥וּ יְהוָ֗ה מַלְאָ֫כָ֥יו גִּבֹּ֣רֵי כֹ֭חַ עֹשֵׂ֣י דְבָר֑וֹ לִ֝שְׁמֹ֗עַ בְּק֣וֹל דְּבָרֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: Bless YHWH, his angels, mighty [ones] of strength, doing his word, by obeying the voice of his word.
pieces: Bless {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, you angels of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}}, strong warriors who carry out what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says and listen for the sound of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} word.

L.20: Bless {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, [you] {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} angels, mighty in strength, who do {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} word, obeying the voice of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} word.

R.20: Angels of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, praise {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}! You are strong and powerful. You do what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says. You obey {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} every word.

decisions.reason: The word (mal'akh) means a messenger; God's messengers in heaven are his angels (91:11).
The word (gibbor) is a warrior, a hero; the angels are the strong ones of God's army (verse 21).

decisions.choice: the call goes out to all
decisions.reason: Having called on himself (verses 1-2), the psalmist calls on the angels, the armies of heaven, and all that God has made (verses 20-22).
As in 103:1, Readable says "praise" for blessing God.

records.source: בָּרֲכ֣וּ יְ֭הוָה כָּל־צְבָאָ֑יו מְ֝שָׁרְתָ֗יו עֹשֵׂ֥י רְצוֹנֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: Bless YHWH, all his hosts, his servants, doing his will.
pieces: Bless {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, all {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} armies, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} attendants who carry out what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} wants.

L.21: Bless {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, all {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hosts, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} servants who do {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} will.

R.21: All the armies of heaven, praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}! You serve {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and do what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} wants.

decisions.choice: his hosts: the armies of heaven
decisions.reason: The hosts (tseva'ot) are God's armies in heaven, his angels and the stars (148:2; 1 Kings 22:19), the word in the title "the LORD of hosts".

decisions.choice: his servants: those who attend him
decisions.reason: The word (meshartim) is used of attendants who wait on a king and of priests who serve in the temple.
As with the title "the LORD of Armies", Balanced and Readable say "armies"; Literal keeps the older "hosts".

records.source: בָּרֲכ֤וּ יְהוָ֨ה׀כָּֽל־מַעֲשָׂ֗יו בְּכָל־מְקֹמ֥וֹת מֶמְשַׁלְתּ֑וֹ בָּרֲכִ֥י נַ֝פְשִׁ֗י אֶת־יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: Bless YHWH, all his works, in all places of his dominion. Bless, my soul, YHWH.
pieces: Bless {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, all that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has made, everywhere under {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} rule. Bless {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, my soul.

L.22: Bless {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, all {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} works, in all places of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} dominion. Bless {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, my soul.

R.22: Everything {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has made, praise {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in every place where {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} rules! With all that I am, I praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: the psalm ends as it began
decisions.reason: The last line repeats the first (verse 1): the call to all creation comes back to the psalmist's own praise.

decisions.choice: his works: all he has made
decisions.reason: All God's works, everything he has made, are called to praise him (145:10; 148).

decisions.choice: With all that I am, I praise the LORD
decisions.reason: As in 103:1.
